title: Adaptive fanout throttling and cache TTL reconciliation to reduce console backend tail latency
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:
The console backend occasionally sees 95th/99th percentile latency spikes during dashboard refresh and multi-entity queries. Investigation points to excessive downstream fanout from the GraphQL resolver layer, redundant REST fetches for the same entity within a request window, and inconsistent TTL configuration between the in-memory prefix cache and Redis-based shared cache.

Goals:
- Introduce adaptive fanout throttling to cap parallel downstream requests per GraphQL operation while preserving latency for small requests.
- Reconcile and document TTL semantics across: per-request prefix cache (in-memory), global Redis cache, and CDN-level cache headers.
- Reduce duplicate REST calls by introducing a request-scoped dedupe layer and migrating hot-fields to memoized resolvers.
- Add focused observability (histograms and top-N call graphs) and a staged rollout plan with traffic shaping.

Deliverables:
1) Throttling middleware (node/ts) injected into resolver execution path with configuration flags and abort semantics.
2) Request-scoped dedupe component used by both GraphQL and legacy REST handlers.
3) Cache TTL matrix and automated config reconciliation script (ci job) to keep envs aligned.
4) Performance dashboards (Datadog) and an incident playbook for fallback to conservative fanout.
5) Migration plan and canary rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic with feature-flag gating.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative throttling can increase P50 for some large analytical requests; mitigation: fast-path whitelist for known bulk endpoints and per-team SLAs.
- Adding dedupe increases memory per request (small map) but reduces overall downstream concurrency and Redis ops.
- Reconciliation script requires runbook coordination with infra for staging and prod config propagation.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th percentile end-to-end latency for dashboard endpoints decreases by at least 30% in canary group
- Downstream request fanout per incoming GraphQL operation reduced by >= 40% for top 20 slowest queries
- No cache inconsistency incidents introduced during rollout (validated by smoke tests)
comments: 2026-02-26 - Triage: Spike authorized. Ava performed initial top-N slow-query analysis and confirmed correlation between fanout and tail latency (Datadog dashboard: https://datadog.company.redwood/dash/console-fanout).

2026-03-02 - Spike update: Implemented a prototype throttling middleware (branch: feat/eng/ENG-564210-throttle-proto). Local replay of 5k synthetic requests showed 48% reduction in max concurrent downstream calls. Marcus to submit PR for code review.
2026-03-05 - Design sync: PM (Rohit Patel) requested explicit escape hatch for high-throughput internal jobs. Decision: add allowlist by route and a token-based bypass for scheduled jobs.

2026-03-07 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1587 contains throttling middleware and request dedupe util. Initial review by @julie-ng and @santiago. Two backend style and one tests comment left.

2026-03-09 - Bench results: Canary harness against staging dataset shows p99 improvement from 1.8s -> 1.2s on problematic dashboard queries. Memory increase per-request measured at ~3.5KB for dedupe map. Good to proceed to canary.

2026-03-11 - Ops note: Added Datadog tracing spans for 'fanout.exec' and 'cache.resolve' to measure effect across services. Dashboard link: https://datadog.company.redwood/dash/console-fanout-v2. Logging format documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Console/ENG-564210+Fanout+and+Cache+Reconciliation

2026-03-12 - Rollout plan approved by SRE and Product. Feature-flag name: ff/eng/564210/adaptive-fanout. Canary to 10% traffic for 24h, monitor errors and latency. Marcus to run the reconciliation script in staging and produce config diff PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/configs/pull/412

2026-03-13 - In-progress: Canary 10% started. Early telemetry: error rate unchanged, p95 down ~22%. Continued monitoring. Planned follow-ups: refine TTL defaults for Redis hot keys and add an automated alert if dedupe map grows beyond threshold.
